decision.trend: Early studies on improving oxidation resistance in high-performance alloys often focused on modifying bulk composition to form protective oxide scales (e.g., by adding reactive elements like Cr or Al). However, more recent works explored surface engineering rather than wholesale composition changes: one effort fused a silicide-based coating (Si–Cr–Fe) to a refractory high-entropy alloy substrate (PMC7475834), another used friction processing to refine surface microstructure for faster, more protective oxide formation (PMC9026100), while a third employed laser cladding to deposit a refractory high-entropy coating with refined phases for better oxidation protection (PMC10142552). These approaches have demonstrated varying degrees of success in forming more stable, adherent oxide layers under high-temperature conditions. Despite progress, challenges remain in fine-tuning processing parameters, ensuring coating adhesion, minimizing coating-induced brittleness, and predicting long-term oxidation performance across broad temperature and environmental ranges.
decision.unsolved: A unified, broadly applicable strategy to identify and optimize oxidation-resistant surface modifications—across different base alloys and service conditions—remains an open challenge, especially without relying primarily on compositional doping. Predictive tools to rationalize or tailor coatings and microstructures for varying conditions are still needed, as are methods to ensure robust coating-substrate adhesion and longevity over the wide range of potential applications.
decision.lever: Develop a machine learning (ML) framework that predicts optimal surface treatment parameters (e.g., composition of slurry/laser clad feeds, friction processing speeds, and process temperatures) for oxidation resistance, using data from existing coating, cladding, and friction-processing studies.
decision.why: Recent work on coatings and friction-based surface engineering has shown promise for improving oxidation resistance without resorting to bulk composition changes. However, the diversity of material systems and oxidation conditions suggests a need for a data-driven solution. An ML-based approach can leverage prior studies’ results to rapidly explore multi-parameter process spaces, guiding the design of optimized surface treatments (e.g., fused slurry recipes, friction-processing speeds, laser cladding conditions) for improved and predictable high-temperature oxidation protection.
